Q: Rust memory ordering and atomics A:

"Happens-before" is something of a misnomer. A more accurate name would be "is-observable-before". IOW if f has side effects, then it is guaranteed that within the same thread g will see those side-effects, and any subsequent code will see both the effects of f and g. However this guarantee disappears between threads: it is possible for another thread to observe the effects of g without seeing the effects of f.

There are two causes why the guarantee disappears between threads:

  • As pointed out by @freakish in a comment, "happens-before" doesn't mean that the operations are physically realized in order: both the compiler and the CPU are allowed to reorder the operations so long as any code that depends on their effects still observes those effects in order.

  • On multi-core systems, it takes time for the effects of operations made by a specific core to become visible on the other cores. And barring memory barriers, there is no guarantee that all effects will travel at the same speed between cores. So even if the originating core ran the operations in order, the effects may become visible out of order in the other cores.

Q: Making calculations in a treelike structure A:

Use reduce(). To get table B from table A:

=let(
  headers; A1:C1;
  data; filter(A2:C; len(C2:C));
  reduce(headers; sequence(rows(data)); lambda(a; i; let(
    row; index(data; i);
    get_; lambda(j; let(
      v; index(row; j);
      b; (j = 3) + (v <> chooserows(tocol(choosecols(a; j); 1); -1));
      if(b; v;)
    ));
    vstack(a; hstack(get_(1); get_(2); get_(3)))
  )))
)

To get table C from table A:

=let(
  headers; A1:C1;
  data; filter(A2:C; len(C2:C));
  spaced; reduce(headers; sequence(rows(data)); lambda(a; i; let(
    row; index(data; i);
    get_; lambda(j; let(
      v; index(row; j);
      b; (j = 3) + (v <> chooserows(tocol(choosecols(a; j); 1); -1));
      blank; iferror(wrapcols(; j - 1;); tocol(; 1));
      vstack(blank; if(b; v;))
    ));
    ifna(vstack(a; hstack(get_(1); get_(2); get_(3))))
  )));
  filter(spaced; byrow(spaced; lambda(r; len(join(; r))))) 
)

Q: Premium requests usage of Copilot and Claude Code plugins in VSCode A:

I’m seeing the same thing and it’s extremely confusing.

I’m using the Claude Code extension from the VS Code sidebar with an active Claude Pro subscription (i.e., I’m not intentionally using Copilot Chat/Agent for the prompts). However:

• The GitHub Copilot Chat panel shows/synchronizes the same conversation history / previous sessions I had in Claude Code.
• After my Claude Pro usage window ended, I checked GitHub billing → Copilot Premium Requests, and I could see Premium Requests being consumed during the period I was using Claude Code in VS Code.

This feels broken: I’m trying to use Anthropic’s service inside VS Code, but somehow GitHub Copilot is also billing me even though Copilot isn’t providing any obvious value in that flow.

Has anyone found a definitive explanation or a way to ensure the Claude Code extension uses only Anthropic billing and does not route through Copilot (or at least does not consume Copilot Premium Requests)?
